SAPS Tubing

By: Viewfinder | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose the apartheid era torture technique which is today prevalent t within the South African Police Service

Unique Selling Point:
Interviews with torture victims, next of kin survivors as well as first and exclusive data finding on the prevalence of torture by SAPS officers - in exposing widespread "tubing" torture allegations against SAPS exposed

Summary:
This story unpacks the case study of a hostel block committee leader who died in police custody, in 2014, heralding an unprecedented wave of political violence in which the SAPS officers were accused of being involved in. Zinakile Fica was allegedly being tortured by an asphyxiation method called "tubing" when he died. We investigate the case: speaking to an anonymous witness, a pathologist who conducted the Fica autopsy, a friend of Fica's who survived "tubing" torture and Fica's widow and hostel- and human rights activist Vanessa Burger. We also bring in perspectives from Peter Jordi, a Johannesburg attorney who has litigated dozens of police torture cases in civil claims.

Further information:
"Tubing" - the act of suffocating a suspect with a plastic bag or an inner tube of a tyre - is a torture method that became synonmous with apartheid's security branch police. But, far from being a relic of the apartheid past, a new investigation by Viewfinder has revealed that the method has permeated the police service and is still in wide use today. A data analysis has revealed more than a thousand instances of tubing complaints from across the country, from every province in cities and rural areas.

In March 2014, Glebelands hostel block committee chairperson Zinakile Fica died in police custody at Isipingo / Prospecton in the south of Durban. Following Fica's death, a deadly wave of political killings engulfed Glebelands, leaving more than 100 people dead. Some police officers would be implicated in facilitating hitmen attacks on block committees. Though Fica's death was written off by investigators as occurring due to natural causes - a "heart attack" - witnesses and an independent private pathologist conclude that Fica was almost certainly being tubed when he died. Fica left behind a wife and a family of five children who were dependent on him as a bread winner. About a year later, one of Fica's friends - Richard Nzama - would be arrested and tortured with this method by police. He survived, and has recounted his ordeal in detail.

People already interviewed on camera: Steve Naidoo (expert pathologist, who conducted autopsy on Fica), Mfanikile Skhosana (witness arrested alongside Fica attests to torture allegations, identity to be obscured), Richard Nzama (torture survivor), Zukiswa Fica (Zinakile wife), Peter Jordi (lawyer with decades experience representing police torture victims), retired Brigadier Clifford Marion (KZN police officer, speaks about apartheid cultures of policing that became embedded in SAPS)

Press Release

Apartheid-style police torture methods in the modern era?
In 2014, Zinakile Fica died in police custody in KwaZulu-Natal. A forensic pathologist concluded that an old apartheid-era asphyxiation method called "tubing" was likely the cause of the heart attack he had suffered. To what extent do police still use this terrifying torture tactic today? An investigation uncovers how some members of the police service are still using this method to torture people in police custody.
Producer: Daneel Knoetze | Camera: Anton Scholtz | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:


Voice over
The last years of apartheid are remembered for political killings, torture and suspicious deaths in police custody. But, for some black, working-class communities in South Africa these issues persist.

Anonymous 1
So I think now, we are moving to the dangerous blocks…

Anonymous 1
C0026
18:35:25:20 - 18:35:30:20
That is the centre where all the killers stay.

Anonymous 1
Many people died here, in these blocks, plenty. In all these blocks.

Link
Between 2014 and 2017, the Glebelands hostel complex in Umlazi saw a spree of political killings. Hitmen roamed these blocks and dozens of people lost their lives. Residents accused some police officers of participating in the violence, instead of curbing it.

Anonymous 1
We are at Block R now.

Anonymous 1
Fica was taken by the police for an interrogation, but they took him violently because he was naked when he was taken here.

Voice over
Zinakile Fica was the chairman of a Glebelands block committee. Committee members say that their opposition to corruption pitted them against the local ward councillor and a murky network of racketeers, hitmen and police officers. Fica’s colleagues believe that his 2014 arrest was politically motivated. Shortly after his arrest, Fica died in police custody. One survivor, arrested along with Fica, has now spoken out.

Anonymous 2
I was in fear, so much fear. That is a day I will never forget in all my life

Anonymous 2
I made a statement because I wanted the law to take its course, and I wanted to help Zinakile Fica’s family for them to know how he died.

Voice over
Like many Glebelands men who have died, Fica was a breadwinner for his family in rural Eastern Cape.

Zukiswa Fica
Zinakile Fica was a kind person, he loved to be around people.

Zukiswa Fica
We had five children.

Zukiswa Fica
He went missing on Thursday, then there was no word.

Zukiswa Fica
I cried. Because, I knew he must be dead.

Voice over
After his arrest, Fica was not taken to the police station. Instead he was brought here.

Link
Glebelands residents say that this office building, in an industrial area near Isipingo beach in Durban, is a black site for police interrogations and torture. It is here where hostel block committee chairman Zinakile Fica died during an interrogation in March 2014.

Anonymous 2
We went in the building, up the stairs to the second floor. We were taken down a dark passage, then we went into a room where we sat down on the floor.

Anonymous 2
Another police officer came in and told us to make sure that we are ready to tell the truth, because otherwise things would turn out bad for us.

Anonymous 2
He opened a drawer and took out folded plastic bags police badges on them with.
He counted the plastics: one, two, three, four.

Anonymous 2
After a few minutes we heard Bhaka (Fica) screaming in the next room.

Voice over
Doctor Steve Naidoo is a forensic pathologist who specialises in deaths in custody and police torture cases. His autopsy report found that Zinakile Fica died from a heart attack, which was likely caused by a police torture method called “tubing”.

MacFarlane Moleli
For the person that’s never heard of this tubing methodology before, what actually is it.

Steve Naidoo
Tubing basically refers to a method of asphyxiation or respiratory obstruction where something is used to block the nostrils, mouth, and the face of a person inducing a very very vulnerable and state of distress.

The tubing term probably arose because of the propensity of the perpetrators to use rubber in a tube of a car, of a vehicle wheel or it could be a hood or a plastic bag.

MacFarlane Moleli
But, Doc, for a police officer who applies this method of torture, what risks are they taking?

Steve Naidoo
What you’re doing is applying an asphyxial stress that is very serious. Now, the problem is there’s a fine line between people that will survive completely and beyond that line that people will die.

Zukiswa Fica
We arrived and we asked the people who worked at the mortuary to see him.
The cover was from the waist down and his upper body was open for us to see him.

Interviewer
Did you not hold him?

Zukiswa Fica
I did not hold him. (crying)

Voice over
Professor Peter Jordi is the head of the Wits Law Clinic in Johannesburg. He has represented scores of torture victims in civil suits against the police.

Peter Jordi
All these are now quite old, you know, they'll be from the 1990s.

Peter Jordi
The one man showing how he was tortured by sitting on the back of the other man.

Peter Jordi
Another one showing how he was hooded and tortured.

Peter Jordi
Naked and bound to a chair and tortured at Brixton Murder and Robbery. They’re all the same, they’re repetitious.

Peter Jordi
After a while, and after 1994, when you would have thought that there would be a reduction in such cases, there was not, there was not a reduction.

Peter Jordi
It seems to have spread more widely.

Voice over
A recent data analysis by investigative journalism unit Viewfinder found more than a thousand individual tubing cases regi stered all across South Africa between 2012 and 2020.

Voice over
According to these complaints, police use the method during interrogations when searching for things like drugs and unlicensed firearms.

Steve Naidoo
Well I have had, a fair amount of experience with living patients, living survivors of torture.

Steve Naidoo
They’ve described to me a state of panic and impending doom: bleeding from the mouth, vomiting, in one or two cases that I had there was incontinence, loss of control of the bladder and the bowel as well

Voice over
Richard Nzama, who also served on the Glebelands block committees, says that he is one such survivor. He was arrested from his place of work as a security guard on the night of 22 July 2015, and driven to a secluded area.

Richard Nzama
The police came with this road with me here and then they just parked the car here. And then they took me here. This is where – are all this place here – where they put the tube on me.

Richard Nzama
This is where they put the tube and then forced me to put my head, see, with the tube, see, inside the water. This is where I peed myself, here, in this place here.

Richard Nzama
I’m still asking myself, how did I manage to, you know, to survive? What was on my mind I was just thinking about Zinakile Fica

MacFarlane Moleli
Boet Richard, maybe just explain to me, how has this case impacted your life?

Richard Nzama
It has affected me because, see i lose my job. Even my life is still standing now see ya. Even now, even though it may be 5 years. I still don’t trust any police. I don’t trust any police. Because each and every time I meet the police or see that police, that image comes back.

MacFarlane Moleli
So, what do you hope for your case, what would you like to see happening at the end?

Richard Nzama
I am still very angry. I just want to see justice take its place.

Link
Since 2012, police in KwaZulu-Natal have been implicated in hundreds of torture cases. But, hardly any of the accused officers have been convicted in court or disciplined by the South African Police Service. Police headquarters in Durban did not agree to our request for an interview.

Voice over
KwaZulu-Natal Police spokesman Brigadier Jay Naicker referred our query to his superior, the national head of communications. But, Major General Mathapelo Peters did not respond to our queries and attempts at following up.

Voice over
The officer implicated in Richard Nzama’s torture was caught out lying to investigators. Yet, he has remained on duty and was even promoted. Matthews Sesoko is the head of investigations at the Independent Police Investigative Directorate. He is now overseeing these investigations.

Matthews Sesoko
There's also another one which also involves the same members who alleged to be involved in Fica and Nzama matter, so those matters will all be presented to the prosecutor as one so they look at the same Modus Operandi and we hope when you look at that probably we’ll have a different outcome in terms of ensuring that the matters are prosecuted.

MacFarlane Moleli
But Mr. Seseko it's taken almost 7 years and surely justice delayed is justice denied.

Matthews Sesoko
That is true and we acknowledge it has taken too long.

MacFarlane Moleli
Where are the police? Are they still on duty? Are they still getting a salary from taxpayers like me? Yet somebody else's life has been messed up on the one hand and another has died.

Matthews Sesoko
That is true and it's very unfortunate such members still continue to be in the system.

Voice over
Zinakile’s youngest son was a baby when his father died. Today he is growing up.

Zukiswa Fica
I tell him that he looks a lot like his father. He asks me “is he as dark as me?” He always hopes that his father will return so that he can see for himself that they look alike.[]



PROMO 1
The use of torture by police is associated with the country’s apartheid past. But, a new investigation has revealed that police torture persists, especially in KwaZulu-Natal.

PROMO 2
The Glebelands hostel in Umlazi is notorious as a haven for hitmen and a site of political killings. But, what of claims that police officers participated in the violence? We investigate the 2014 death in police custody of a block committee chairperson, alleged to have been tortured by members of the South African Police Service.

PROMO 3

In 2014, a hostel block committee chairperson from Umlazi died during a police interrogation at this office building in Durban's industrial south. We investigate allegations that tubing - a torture method popular during apartheid - played a role in his death.
Peter Jordi
After a while, and after 1994, when you would have thought that there would be a reduction in such cases there was not a reduction.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Interviews with torture victims, next of kin survivors as well as first and exclusive data finding on the prevalence of torture by SAPS officers - in exposing widespread "tubing" torture allegations against SAPS exposed
metadata.Summary: This story unpacks the case study of a hostel block committee leader who died in police custody, in 2014, heralding an unprecedented wave of political violence in which the SAPS officers were accused of being involved in. Zinakile Fica was allegedly being tortured by an asphyxiation method called "tubing" when he died. We investigate the case: speaking to an anonymous witness, a pathologist who conducted the Fica autopsy, a friend of Fica's who survived "tubing" torture and Fica's widow and hostel- and human rights activist Vanessa Burger. We also bring in perspectives from Peter Jordi, a Johannesburg attorney who has litigated dozens of police torture cases in civil claims.
metadata.Further information: "Tubing" - the act of suffocating a suspect with a plastic bag or an inner tube of a tyre - is a torture method that became synonmous with apartheid's security branch police. But, far from being a relic of the apartheid past, a new investigation by Viewfinder has revealed that the method has permeated the police service and is still in wide use today. A data analysis has revealed more than a thousand instances of tubing complaints from across the country, from every province in cities and rural areas. In March 2014, Glebelands hostel block committee chairperson Zinakile Fica died in police custody at Isipingo / Prospecton in the south of Durban. Following Fica's death, a deadly wave of political killings engulfed Glebelands, leaving more than 100 people dead. Some police officers would be implicated in facilitating hitmen attacks on block committees. Though Fica's death was written off by investigators as occurring due to natural causes - a "heart attack" - witnesses and an independent private pathologist conclude that Fica was almost certainly being tubed when he died. Fica left behind a wife and a family of five children who were dependent on him as a bread winner. About a year later, one of Fica's friends - Richard Nzama - would be arrested and tortured with this method by police. He survived, and has recounted his ordeal in detail. People already interviewed on camera: Steve Naidoo (expert pathologist, who conducted autopsy on Fica), Mfanikile Skhosana (witness arrested alongside Fica attests to torture allegations, identity to be obscured), Richard Nzama (torture survivor), Zukiswa Fica (Zinakile wife), Peter Jordi (lawyer with decades experience representing police torture victims), retired Brigadier Clifford Marion (KZN police officer, speaks about apartheid cultures of policing that became embedded in SAPS)
